etym.s: fr. 1. कि, originally nom. and acc. sg. n. of 2. क॑, q.v.

spans.s: , what? how? whence? wherefore? why?

is much used as a particle of interrogation like the Lat. num, an, sometimes translatable by ‘whether?’ but oftener serving only like a note of interrogation to mark a question (e.g. किं व्याधा वने ऽस्मिन् संचरन्ति, ‘do hunters roam about in this wood?’ In an interrogation the verb, if uncompounded with a preposition, generally retains its accent after किम्, Pāṇ. viii, 1, 44). To this sense may be referred the किम् expressing inferiority, deficiency, &c. at the beginning of compounds (e.g. किं-राजन्, what sort of king? i.e. a bad king, Pāṇ. ii, 1, 64; v, 4, 70)
also the किम् prefixed to verbs with a similar meaning (e.g. किम्-अधीते, he reads badly, Pāṇ. viii, 1, 44,Kāś.) किम्—उत, or किम्—उत-वा or किम्—अथवा—उत, whether—or—or, R.; Śak.; Bhartṛ. &c. (cf. उत॑.)
is very frequently connected with other particles, as follows: कि॑म् अङ्ग॑, wherefore then? RV.
किम्. See अ॑थ
अपि, somewhat, to a considerable extent, rather, much more, still further, Śak.; Megh. &c.
इति, why? Śak.; Kum.; Pañcat. &c.
किम्-इव, what for? Śiś. xvi, 31
or कि॑म्-उत॑ how much more? how much less? RV.; ŚBr.; MBh. &c.
किल, what a pity! (expressing dissatisfaction), Pāṇ. iii, 3, 146
किं-च, moreover, further, Pañcat.; Kathās. &c.
what more (expressing impatience), Śak.
(originally -च न, negative = ‘in no way’), to a certain degree, a little, Kathās.
(with a negation) in no way, not at all, MBh. i, 6132
किं-चिद्, somewhat, a little, MBh.; R. &c.
तर्हि, how then? but, however, Pāṇ. ii, 2, 4, Pat.; iv, 1, 163, Kāś.
किं-तु, but, however, nevertheless (bearing the same relation to तु that किं-च bears to च), MBh.; R. &c.
किं-नु, whether indeed? (a stronger interrogative than किम् alone), MBh.; R. &c.
how much more? how much less? Bhag. i, 35
नु खलु, how possibly? (a still stronger interrogative), Śak.
पुनर्, how much more? how much less? R.; Bhag. ix, 33 &c.
however, Bālar.
but, ib.
वा, whether? or whether? Śak.; Pañcat. &c.
or (often a mere particle of interrogation)
स्विद्, why? Kathās. xxvi, 75
a stronger interrogative than किम् alone, RV.; MBh.; Kathās.

किम्—पुरुष॑ -पुरुष॑ [ŚBr. i] or -पु॑रुष [ŚBr. vii], m. ‘what sort of a man?’ a mongrel being (according to the Brāhmaṇas an evil being similar to man; perhaps originally a kind of monkey [cf. BhP. xi, 16, 29]; in later times the word is usually identified with किं-नर, though sometimes applied to other beings in which the figure of a man and that of an animal are combined; these beings are supposed to live on Hema-kūṭa and are regarded as the attendants of Kubera; with Jains the Kimpuruṣas, like the Kiṃnaras, belong to the Vyantaras)
N. of one of the nine sons of Āgnīdhra (having the Varṣa Kimpuruṣa as his hereditary portion), VP.

a division of the earth (one of the nine Khaṇḍas or portions into which the earth is divided, and described as the country between the Himācala and Hema-kūṭa mountains, also called किम्पुरुष-वर्ष, Kād.), VP.; BhP.; MatsyaP. &c.
